newsitem.title: USA: Somanetics gets rights to new products.
newsitem.headline: Somanetics gets rights to new products.

text.p: Somanetics Corp said Monday it has become the commercialization partner of NeuroPhysics Corp, a Groton, Mass.-based research and development company.

NeuroPhysics is currently conducting research into the feasibility and development of prototypes for four new products related to Somanetics' business and its INVOS technology, which non-invasively measures blood oxygen saturation in the brain.
Somanetics said it will have significant ownership rights and an exclusive worldwide license for the commercialization of these products and to any related new technology.

Somanetics said the U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity just awarded NeuroPhysics a $500,000 Phase II contract to develop and test models of devices that use noninvasive in vivo near-infrared spectroscopy for several applications.

The applications include: a liver oxygenation monitor for assessing and controlling shock caused by loss of blood in accident victims and battlefield casualties; a device for locating and assessing subdural hematomas (internal bleeding between skull and brain) in head trauma patients; and a blood gas monitor.
The Phase II contract follows a $70,000 Phase I contract which demonstrated the feasibility of this technology for these applications.

Additionally, NeuroPhysics also has received a $100,000 Phase I contract from the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke to investigate the feasibility of using a in vivo near infrared spectroscopy for continuously monitoring fetal cerebral oxygenation during labor and delivery.
